chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Any free woman who marries herself to a slave without the permission of his master has legalized her private parts, and there is no dower for her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal consequence for a free woman who marries a slave without her master's permission?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'nikah al-mu'allaq' (conditional marriage) for a free woman marrying a slave without her master's consent, ruling that the marriage is valid but she forfeits her dower (mahr) as a penalty for the lack of permission. It highlights the master's authority over the economic aspects of the slave's union and reflects the socio-economic realities of early Islamic society where slave ownership influenced marital contracts. The ruling underscores the principle that while the marital bond is established, the financial rights are contingent upon the master's approval.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whichever free woman marries herself to a slave without a permission of his master, so she has legalized her private parts and there is no dower for her’.
